terra.problem: The text does not say nobody stood apart with crossed arms.
The text does not describe the whole neighborhood or say nobody objected.
The explanation repeats the answer without a distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The text does not say whether an uncle gets a vote.
The text does not say Elizabeth spoke loudly.
The claim that John keeps the name for the rest of the story goes beyond this passage without a reference.
The explanation is generic and ends by simply pointing back to the verse.
The text does not identify family tradition as the reason for their response or say Elizabeth is about to challenge it.
Papa says he was unable to speak in the drawer, but his backstory says he spoke to and welcomed others there.
The text does not say Zechariah is not going anywhere.
The text says everyone was amazed, not that they had nothing left to argue about.
The text does not say the relatives had done plenty of questioning.
The text does not say the neighbors are standing there or identify whom Zechariah speaks to first.
The explanation invents a room and says what the hearers are thinking beyond the question the text gives.
Aaron is not identified as Israel's first priest in Exodus 28:1, and the claim about Zechariah being a priest's namesake is unsupported.
The explanation is a generic elimination followed by a restatement of the answer.
David being a king needs a reference outside the passage, and the text does not say Zechariah's purpose is to push kings out.
Saying John gets a road ready turns preparing the way into a physical road-building job, which the text does not state.
The reference to Papa's experience of darkness needs to identify the drawer so a baker unfamiliar with his backstory can understand it.
The text does not say John became strong in spirit in the wilderness or describe his years there as quiet.
The text does not say John's growing up happened in the wilderness.
The text says John lived in the wilderness until his public appearance; it does not say he waited there for that day.
